metadata.description: Single-plugin marketplace exposing the cc-enslaver discipline plugin.

plugins.name: cc-enslaver
plugins.description: Rules your coding agent physically cannot ignore. A Claude Code plugin (and LLM-agnostic rule pack) that stops reactive patching, guessed citations, surface-level fixes and premature "done" claims by intercepting the agent's own tool calls rather than asking it nicely. PreToolUse denies an edit before it lands — editing a file you never opened this session, a suppression marker with no adjacent why-comment, a hardcoded secret or user-home path, the fourth small patch to one file, a dangerous shell flag. A nine-layer Stop gate then refuses to let a completion claim end the turn without evidence, a convergence self-quiz, a fidelity check against the user's ORIGINAL request, and a one-line TL;DR. Twelve rules, eight backed by a hook; "Imperial Edict" regexes you define per project; a repo-wide sync gate; three CI drift gates that derive every documented number from the code so the documentation cannot rot. Zero dependencies, stdlib only, Linux + Windows CI, and every guard fails OPEN — a bug in the discipline can never brick your agent. v0.30.0 is a structural audit of the plugin itself, on one theme: a thing that is written down is not a thing that is enforced. Seven unreachable production symbols were deleted rather than annotated, among them a retired rationale checker left standing beside the live one — where the next reader has no way to tell which of the two the guard actually consults — and an `_escape_triple_quoted` marked "kept only so an external caller does not break" that no caller could reach. Three duplicated judgements were collapsed to one definition each: markdown fence parsing existed in three copies, each carrying its own transcription of the same v0.25 CommonMark fix, and the project-root predicate existed twice with the second annotated "same project-root heuristic as lib/edicts.py" — a comment that names an invariant without holding it, so widening one copy silently leaves the other behind (new shared module: lib/projroot.py). And the Stop status table stopped making a claim of its own kind: layers are DISPLAYED (a) through (i) but EVALUATED with (b) first, because a hedge invalidates a done-claim however much evidence sits beside it — yet the table derived both "Pass" and "pending" from the display index, so every hedge block printed "(a) PASS", asserting that convergence evidence had been found on a turn where `_has_evidence` was never called. A gate built to catch unfounded claims does not get to make one; fixed, with twin tests in both directions. The file tree was reclassified rather than rearranged: test files are named for what they cover and indexed file-by-file in tests/README.md, hooks/scripts/ labels its three roles inline, and docs/ gained an index. The four non-hook scripts deliberately did NOT move into a tools/ directory — gc_state.py is imported by inject_context.py for auto-GC and register_read.py's real logic lives inside bash_guard.py, so neither is a standalone CLI and the move would trade a tidier directory name for a real cross-tree sys.path splice. CLAUDE.md shrank from 87 KB to 39 KB: its "current version" section had grown into a verbatim second copy of the changelog, re-read into context on every single session and free to drift from the original. 564 → 565 tests, all green on Linux and Windows. Full release history lives in CHANGELOG.md, which is now its only copy.
